messages:
emma: Heads up — hitting a weird issue in the Kotlin SDK around suspending Retrofit wrappers + multipart uploads. Repro in sampleapp. When an auth 401 happens mid-upload the suspend wrapper returns error and the original request isn't retried. Java callback path retries after token refresh. Anyone seen this?

alex: Hmm can you paste the minimal repro + okhttp/version + Android API level?

emma: Quick details: Retrofit 2.9, OkHttp 4.11.0, our suspend wrapper that wraps Call.enqueue -> suspend. Repro in sampleapp on Pixel 6 (Android 13) and Pixel 2 (Android 9) — only fails on 13. Repro link: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapp/repro/multipart-suspend (internal).

sam: Sounds like the RequestBody might not be repeatable. Java path likely clones the Call or rebuilds the body on retry, whereas the suspend helper might be reusing the exhausted call. Do your logs show something like 'stream closed' or 'RequestBody content exhausted'?

emma: Logs: "401 Unauthorized" then "java.io.IOException: closed" during writeTo. Short trace: okhttp3.internal.http2.StreamAllocation:streamFailed -> okio.ForwardingSink.write -> java.io.IOException: closed.

priya: Quick workaround: make the multipart RequestBody repeatable by buffering it. Example pattern: ```kotlin
val buffered = object : RequestBody() {
  override fun contentType() = multipart.contentType()
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) {
    val buf = Buffer()
    multipart.writeTo(buf)
    sink.writeAll(buf)
  }
  override fun contentLength() = buf.size
}
``` Expensive but avoids one-shot bodies.

alex: Also check that our suspend adapter calls `call.clone()` before enqueueing for retries. If it reuses the same Call instance the underlying request stream will be gone after first attempt.

emma: We do `call.awaitResponse()` which uses `call.enqueue`. Looking at helper: we keep a reference to the original Call and don't clone on retry. Ok will try cloning per-execution.

joe: This looks like an SDK parity bug: Java samples implicitly or explicitly clone the call in auth retry interceptor; Kotlin suspend helper missed that. Fix should be: on each execution call `call.clone()` and execute that. Also detect non-repeatable bodies and log a clear warning pointing to docs.

sam: I'll open a tiny PR to make the suspend adapter clone the call for each run and add a failing test that simulates a 401 mid-stream. @emma can you drop a minimal repro (just the multipart + fake auth server) so we can attach to the test?

emma: Will add a repro branch and attach logs + device matrix. For now I'll add a note in onboarding docs about "use repeatable RequestBody for long uploads or prefer Java callback path until fix" :pray:

devops-bot: deploy-bot: CI build for PR #1234 succeeded :white_check_mark:

priya: Also file an internal ticket to consider shipping a `RepeatableRequestBody` util in the SDK so sample apps don't need to copy/paste this buffering wrapper.

emma: Filed INF-4321: https://issues.internal/redwood/INF-4321 (internal).

alex: Thanks all — moving to backlog for proper fix + test matrix across API levels. Assigning @sam to follow up.
